# 2. Log-Transform Variables

Since we already determined variables were not normally distributed, we just need to log-transform them.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Exclude the following variables from being log-transformed
exclude_vars <- c(
  "pH",
  "Relative_elevation_m",
  "Developed_lulc"
)

# Helper function
add_log_variables <- function(dat, exclude_vars) {

  dat %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        .cols = where(is.numeric) &
          !any_of(exclude_vars) &
          !starts_with("log_"),     
        .fns  = ~ ifelse(.x > 0, log10(.x), NA_real_),
        .names = "log_{.col}"
      )
    )
}

# Run
ha10_cs <- add_log_variables(ha10_cs, exclude_vars)
ha10_os <- add_log_variables(ha10_os, exclude_vars)
ha80_cs <- add_log_variables(ha80_cs, exclude_vars)

# Check
names(ha10_cs)[grepl("^log_", names(ha10_cs))]
```

Export transformed variables to excel by creating a second version of the clean Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Create a new workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# Add worksheets
addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10% Closed System")
addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10% Open System")
addWorksheet(wb, "HA 80% Closed System")

# Write data to each sheet
writeData(wb, sheet = "HA 10% Closed System", ha10_cs)
writeData(wb, sheet = "HA 10% Open System",  ha10_os)
writeData(wb, sheet = "HA 80% Closed System", ha80_cs)

# Save to current working directory
saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean2.xlsx",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```
